title: Show the address space of IPv6 addresses
description: The first few bits of an IPv6 address are defined by [RFC 4291 section 2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291#section-2.4) to define its address space. This MR allows a user to opt in to seeing the address space of IPv6 source and destination addresses by enabling a preference.

I don't think mushing everything into an "address type" field is appropriate. Type roughly corresponds to the the [address space](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xhtml). The others roughly correspond to the [special address registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xhtml) and should be separate.

Why not use FT_STRING instead of FT_UINT8 for these generated fields?

Let's not go crazy with the warnings for special purpose addresses. I have used special purpose addresses like documentation and others for test purposes and being blasted with warnings is annoying and unhelpful.

> I don't think mushing everything into an "address type" field is appropriate. Type roughly corresponds to the the [address space](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xhtml). The others roughly correspond to the [special address registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/ipv6-address-space/ipv6-address-space.xhtml) and should be separate.

When I started this work, I was going from the original IPv6 RFC which defined address types based on specific bit patterns at the start of the address. As I've been informed by you and your fellow volunteers of updated information, the "address type" moniker has become a bit rough.

I'll note that you also use the word "rough" when citing possible alternative approaches. So I guess the question becomes, is this change useful at all, if it can't be clearly defined and labelled? Do you think there's value in this information, or should we just save each others' time and close this MR?

> Why not use FT_STRING instead of FT_UINT8 for these generated fields?

I used FT_UINT8 with a `value_string` because it's a small range of possibilities. It behaves the same as a FT_STRING field to the end user, since I've used BASE_NONE for the fields, and lets Wireshark deal with string allocation and deallocation as it sees fit. The calculus may change, depending on whether/how this MR is made acceptable.

> Let's not go crazy with the warnings for special purpose addresses. I have used special purpose addresses like documentation and others for test purposes and being blasted with warnings is annoying and unhelpful.

Roger that, I'll remove it if work is to continue here.

The reference here is [RFC 4291 Section 2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291.html#section-2.4).

One issue is that a special-purpose range is a subset of type. Your change as implemented cannot express that.

I think adding the address space type (Global Unicast/Multicast/ULA/Link-local) is useful. The others I'm not sure if they deserve their own field ("special-purpose type") or should be handled on a case-by-case basis (teredo information already exists for example).

There is a tension between adding potentially useful information and hurting usability for 99% of use cases with noise. I haven't considered the design aspect of it yet but we should.

> The reference here is [RFC 4291 Section 2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4291.html#section-2.4).

Can you please explain the purpose of calling out the first reference I cited in this MR's summary? Someone on the Discord (possibly it was even yourself) provided that reference when I was earlier in my work on this change. If you can access the edit history of the MR's summary, you'll be able to find the exact date when I switched to that from [RFC 2373 section 2.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2373#section-2.4), but even if you can't, you may be able to find it in my commit history, assuming the squashing didn't obliterate it.

> One issue is that a special-purpose range is a subset of type. Your change as implemented cannot express that.

I've demonstrated my willingness to make changes to my MR -- that's the whole point of having MRs, after all -- and that willingness continues; I'd just like to know that there is a light at the end of the tunnel to work toward. If you feel that focusing solely on address space type is the best approach, then I'll do that. I also like that idea from a design standpoint, because it's clearer and easier to understand than my previous proposals.

> Can you please explain the purpose of calling out the first reference I cited in this MR's summary?

It was just a call out. Nevermind.

> I've demonstrated my willingness to make changes to my MR -- that's the whole point of having MRs, after all -- and that willingness continues; I'd just like to know that there is a light at the end of the tunnel to work toward.

This is an iterative two-way process. I may not necessarily immediately have all the answers to my objections and concerns. I have considered adding this information before and I didn't because I wasn't sure how to do it effectively but I'm not against it.

Having said that I think you should remove Documentation, remove Teredo, and add a preference that encompasses the IPv6 address properties subtree.

After this is merged we can consider how to add back special-purpose and multicast scope address types.
Sounds good to me! Thank you for working with me on this. And thanks for your patience while I figure things out (and not just things in the code).

The work is done. It's all behind a preference as you requested, so it won't bother anyone. And I moved it to its own function, which doesn't even get called if the preference isn't set, so the changes to `add_ipv6_address()` are minimal.

For example using an IPv6 documentation address range for Wireshark screenshots, possibly in a crafted packet, would be an excellent use for these addresses, but with your warning this use case is eliminated (without spurious warnings).

commits_data.title: Show the address spaces of IPv6 addresses
commits_data.message:
Show the address spaces of IPv6 addresses

Add a field which shows the IPv6 source or destination
address space:

* The unspecified address (::/128)
* Loopback (::1/128)
* Multicast (FF00::/8)
* Link-local unicast (FE80::/10)
* Global unicast (2000::/3)
* Reserved by IETF (none of the above)

Future work could expand on this change by adding additional parsing of
the address field based on its space. (For example, multicast addresses
have a defined structure which includes flag bits, a scope field, and a
group identifier.)
